root_idea.summary: The root centers on a peg or stake fixed in the ground or a wall, with related ideas of firmness, stabilization, and peg-like projection.
root_idea.development: The lexical field extends from fixing a physical peg to becoming firm, making something secure, and figuratively naming supports or prominent projections. The Quranic image of mountains as pegs applies this stabilizing image to the earth.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural is normalized under the singular dictionary citation form وَتِدٌ.

senses.definition: A peg or stake fixed in the ground or a wall.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural أَوْتَاد. It denotes stakes or pegs in the ordinary physical sense, including the stake imagery of 38:12 and 89:10.

senses.definition: A mountain conceived as a peg that steadies or secures the earth.
senses.usage_conditions: In 78:7, the mountains are described through the peg image; the associated explanation is that they make the earth firm or secure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hammer in, fix, or make fast a wooden pin, peg, or stake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be fixed in the ground or in a wall; the action includes striking it with a mallet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fixed, firm, or fast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figuratively, the use can describe standing firmly, remaining settled in a place, or growing grain becoming firm and strong.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make firm or secure by fixing, especially to stabilize the earth by means of mountains.
To become sexually aroused or have an erection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative sexual usage associated with the Form II verbal noun تَوْتِيدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A supporting thing or confirming word used to corroborate speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported dialectal or figurative expression; the source presents the item as something by which speech is reinforced.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The chiefs or leading figures of towns, provinces, or countries.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural application of the peg or support image.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The teeth, conceived as pegs of the mouth.
The projecting part of a sandal's ear or loop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical or structural part of the sandal described by resemblance to a peg.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In prosody, a division of a metrical foot consisting of three letters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be a conjoined peg, وَتِدٌ مَقْرُونٌ, or a disjoined peg, وَتِدٌ مَفْرُوقٌ. The metrical foot depends on it, so زِحَاف does not affect it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A prominent peg-like part of the ear, including the tragus or a related inner projection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical descriptions include the prominent anterior part and the two inner ear projections resembling a peg.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Standing fixed, firm, or motionless; erect, as of a horn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or descriptive active-participle usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fixing or making firm a wooden pin, peg, or stake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial usage referring to the fixing action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wooden pin, peg, or stake that has been fixed or made firm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-result description of the fixed object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mallet used to knock wooden pins, pegs, or stakes into the ground or a wall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related form مِيتَدٌ is also reported.
